# Kite

> A small, explicit language for the web, compiled to WebAssembly. Kite is new
> and is in no model's training data, so anything an LLM writes from memory is
> a guess. The compiler is a 2 MB WebAssembly module on npm — check the guess
> instead of shipping it.

Run this before believing any Kite you read or write. No install, no toolchain,
works in a sandbox:

```
npx --yes @kite-lang/compiler-wasm kitec check program.kite
```

`kitec --explain E0302` prints the reasoning behind any diagnostic code.

## Start here

- [Skill](https://kite-lang.dev/skill/SKILL.md): the whole language for an agent, in one file. Every example in it and in its references is compiled by the real compiler as a condition of being written down. Start here rather than with the specification — this is the delta from what a Rust or TypeScript programmer would assume, which is where the mistakes are.
- [Everything, concatenated](https://kite-lang.dev/llms-full.txt): the skill and all six of its reference pages in one document, for a single fetch.

## The language

- [Specification](https://kite-lang.dev/SPECIFICATION.md): normative, sixteen sections. Types, error handling, traits, generics, concurrency, modules, the memory model and the host boundary.
- [Grammar](https://kite-lang.dev/docs/05-grammar.ebnf): the complete EBNF.
- [README](https://kite-lang.dev/README.md): what Kite is for and what it refuses to do.

## Reference, generated from the library's own source

- [Skill reference pages](https://kite-lang.dev/skill/references/index.md): lexical and types, declarations and control flow, errors, structs through generics, concurrency through the host boundary, and the standard library with the toolchain.
- [Standard library](https://kite-lang.dev/reference.html): twenty modules, written in Kite. `dom`, `window`, `html` and `js` are web-only.

## Things worth knowing before writing any

- An error cannot be thrown away by a bare call, and `(T, error)` is fallibility rather than a tuple return.
- A line ending a complete expression ends the statement; a continued expression carries its operator at the end of the line.
- A module is a directory **or** a single `.kite` file, and neither is a module until a `use` names it. A module reaches only what it imports.
- There is no overloading, no default argument, no variadic, no turbofish, no module-level `var`, and no command-line argument of any kind.

## Optional

- [Playground](https://kite-lang.dev/playground.html): the compiler itself, running in the page.
- [Install](https://kite-lang.dev/install.md): the native toolchain, for a machine rather than an agent.
- [Design notes](https://kite-lang.dev/docs/index.md): the research behind the platform, concurrency and compiler decisions.
